high.title: Indonesia Secures US$17 Billion Commitment from AIIB, Finance Minister Says It's Not Debt
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa has received a US$17 billion (Rp 303 trillion) funding commitment from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), a China-backed multilateral lender. The minister clarified this is project financing rather than sovereign debt, to be used for productive infrastructure projects at below-market interest rates, with funds drawable through 2029. This is a significant capital inflow that could boost infrastructure development and reduce reliance on conventional government borrowing.

high.title: Trump Furious: US Strikes Iran Again, Raising Concerns Over Strait of Hormuz Oil Trade Route
high.summary: The United States has launched new military strikes against Iran, targeting missile storage sites, drone facilities, and coastal radar installations, after accusing Iran of violating a ceasefire agreement in the Strait of Hormuz. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical global oil shipping lane, and renewed tensions could disrupt oil supply and drive up global energy prices. This development is highly relevant for Indonesia as it may impact oil import costs, fuel subsidies, and energy sector stocks.

high.title: Finance Minister Calls for Significant Budget Cuts to Free Nutritious Meal Program (MBG)
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa confirmed significant budget efficiencies are being applied to the government's flagship Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) program, stating he ideally wanted to cut the budget to zero but acknowledged the program's social value. He urged the National Nutrition Agency (BGN) to improve implementation to justify the spending. This signals continued fiscal consolidation efforts by the government, which could affect the state budget outlook and related sectors.

high.title: Root Cause: US Attacks Iran, Singapore Ship Shot in Strait of Hormuz
high.summary: US military (CENTCOM) launched strikes against Iran on Friday June 26, targeting missile storage sites, drone depots, and coastal radar positions, in retaliation for Iran's attack on a Singapore-flagged vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz. This escalation poses significant risks to global shipping routes and oil supply chains, as the Strait of Hormuz is a critical chokepoint for approximately 20% of global oil trade. Indonesian businesses and investors should monitor potential crude oil price spikes and supply chain disruptions that could impact domestic fuel prices and inflation.

high.title: Trump Threatens 100% Tariff on Countries That Tax US Digital Companies
high.summary: US President Donald Trump announced via Truth Social that he will impose 100% retaliatory tariffs on any country that levies taxes on US digital companies, effectively overriding existing trade agreements. This directly threatens Indonesia, which has been developing a digital services tax framework that could affect US tech giants operating in the country. Indonesian exporters face potential severe trade disruption, and the government may need to reassess its digital tax policy to avoid damaging its trade relationship with the United States.

high.title: Iran's IRGC Issues Stern Warning to Ships Traveling Outside Official Strait of Hormuz Routes
high.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard (IRGC) warned all commercial vessels to strictly follow Tehran-designated shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz, threatening action against ships using unauthorized routes established without Iranian coordination. This signals Iran's intent to maintain control over the critical waterway despite the existing US-Iran peace deal, creating significant uncertainty for global shipping operators. The development could drive up shipping insurance premiums and freight costs, with downstream effects on Indonesian import prices and trade logistics.

high.title: Trump Furious: US Strikes Iran Again Over Strait of Hormuz Ceasefire Violations
high.summary: US President Donald Trump ordered military strikes on Iranian missile storage facilities, drone sites, and coastal radar installations on June 25, citing Iran's violation of the Strait of Hormuz ceasefire agreement. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical global oil trade route, and renewed conflict there poses significant risks to global oil supply and prices. Indonesian investors should monitor potential commodity price spikes and Rupiah volatility driven by rising geopolitical risk premiums.

high.title: Indonesia Secures US$17 Billion Commitment from AIIB — Finance Minister Says It's Not Debt
high.summary: Indonesian Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa announced a US$17 billion (approximately Rp 303 trillion) financing commitment from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), a China-backed multilateral lender headquartered in Beijing. The minister clarified the funds constitute project financing rather than sovereign debt, to be deployed for productive infrastructure projects at below-market interest rates, with disbursements available through 2029. This is a major capital inflow signal for Indonesian infrastructure sectors and could influence sovereign credit sentiment and Rupiah dynamics.

high.title: Antam Gold Price Falls Rp 8,000 Per Gram Over the Week; Buyback Price Drops Rp 20,000
high.summary: Antam 24-karat gold prices ended the trading week of June 22–27, 2026 down Rp 8,000 per gram, closing at Rp 2,660,000 per gram after opening the week at Rp 2,668,000. The buyback price fell more steeply by Rp 20,000 per gram, reflecting a volatile week that saw a mid-week drop of Rp 18,000 on Wednesday before a partial recovery. This is relevant to retail investors holding gold as a safe-haven asset, particularly given concurrent geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

high.title: US Attacks Iran Again: Here's the Root Cause
high.summary: The US launched retaliatory strikes against Iran after Iranian forces attacked a Singapore-flagged cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz, violating a ceasefire agreement. US Central Command targeted Iranian missile storage facilities, drone sites, and coastal radar installations. This escalation threatens global energy supply chains and shipping routes, with potential impact on oil prices and Indonesian trade flows through the critical Hormuz corridor.

high.title: Chicken Prices at Farms Free-Fall to IDR 13,000/kg While Production Costs Reach IDR 22,000-23,000/kg
high.summary: Farm-gate chicken prices have collapsed to IDR 13,000/kg in West Java, far below the production cost of IDR 22,000-23,000/kg, causing severe losses for small-scale poultry farmers since April 2026. The crisis is compounded by the school holiday period and the temporary suspension of the government's free nutritious meals (MBG) program, which has reduced demand. Industry group Permindo is urging the government to reinstate chicken and egg social assistance programs covering 1.5 million recipients to help absorb excess supply.

high.title: Government Collects Rp 52.85 Trillion from Crypto and P2P Lending Taxes
high.summary: Indonesia's Directorate General of Taxes (DJP) has accumulated Rp 52.85 trillion in state revenue from the digital economy sector as of May 31, 2026. The breakdown includes Rp 40.55 trillion from e-commerce VAT (PPN PMSE), Rp 2.06 trillion from crypto asset taxes, Rp 4.98 trillion from fintech/P2P lending taxes, and Rp 5.26 trillion from government procurement system taxes. This signals the government's growing capacity to tax digital businesses and may indicate further regulatory tightening for digital finance players operating in Indonesia.

high.title: Chicken Prices Crash to Rp 13,000/kg at Farm Level, Farmers in Crisis
high.summary: Farm-gate chicken prices have plummeted to Rp 13,000/kg in West Java, far below the production cost of Rp 22,000–23,000/kg, causing severe losses for independent poultry farmers since April 2026. The crisis is compounded by school holidays halting the Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) program, reducing demand significantly. Farmers are urging the government to reinstate chicken and egg social assistance programs for 1.5 million beneficiaries to help absorb supply and stabilize prices in the poultry sector.

high.title: Revealed: The Root Cause of the US Attacking Iran Again
high.summary: US President Donald Trump ordered retaliatory strikes against Iran on June 25, 2026, after Iranian forces attacked a Singapore-flagged cargo vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, violating the ceasefire agreement between the two nations. US Central Command targeted Iranian missile storage facilities, drone sites, and coastal radar installations. This escalation poses significant risks to global commodity prices, shipping costs, and the Indonesian Rupiah, as the Strait of Hormuz is a critical corridor for oil trade that directly impacts Indonesia's energy imports and export revenues.

medium.title: PLN Coal Supply Situation Revealed: 141 Million MT Secured Out of 154 Million MT Annual Needs
medium.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM) disclosed that approximately 141 million metric tons of coal have been secured for state electricity company PLN out of a total annual requirement of 154 million MT. The ministry had temporarily halted coal exports to prioritize domestic power plant supply, but exports have since returned to normal. This is relevant for coal sector investors as it highlights the government's willingness to restrict exports to ensure domestic energy security.

medium.title: MRT Route from Lebak Bulus to Serpong Kept Secret to Prevent Land Speculation
medium.summary: The Indonesian government is keeping the exact route of the planned MRT Jakarta extension from Lebak Bulus to Serpong, South Tangerang, confidential to prevent land brokers from driving up property prices along the corridor. The feasibility study for the project is targeted for completion by end of 2026. Investors in South Tangerang property and infrastructure-related stocks should monitor this project closely as the route announcement could trigger significant land value movements.

medium.title: Antam Gold Price Rises Slightly, Buyback Price Jumps Rp 38,000 per Gram
medium.summary: Antam 24-karat gold prices rose Rp 5,000 per gram to Rp 2,660,000 after two days of stagnation, while the buyback price surged Rp 38,000 per gram. Over the past week, Antam gold traded in the range of Rp 2,655,000–2,673,000 per gram, while the monthly range stood at Rp 2,799,000–2,803,000 per gram. The price movement reflects global safe-haven demand likely driven by rising geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, which is relevant for Indonesian retail investors holding gold as an asset.

medium.title: Finance Minister Purbaya on Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) Budget Efficiency: 'I Wanted Zero, But That's Not Possible'
medium.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa confirmed that significant budget cuts will be made to the Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) program, stating the reduction is 'quite significant' and will improve overall state budget safety. While he acknowledged the program's social value, he urged the National Nutrition Agency (BGN) to improve implementation efficiency. This signals continued fiscal consolidation efforts by the government, which is relevant for investors monitoring Indonesia's fiscal health and public spending trajectory.

medium.title: Coal Supply for PLN Revealed: 141 Million Metric Tons Secured Out of 154 Million MT Annual Need
medium.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM) disclosed that approximately 141 million metric tons of coal have been secured for state electricity company PLN against an annual requirement of 154 million MT, leaving a roughly 13 million MT gap. The ministry had temporarily halted coal exports to prioritize domestic energy supply, but exports have since returned to normal. This update is relevant to coal mining sector investors (e.g., ADRO, PTBA, ITMG) as domestic market obligation (DMO) enforcement and export restrictions directly impact revenue.

medium.title: MRT Lebak Bulus–Serpong Route Kept Secret to Prevent Land Speculation
medium.summary: Indonesia's Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandhi confirmed that the exact route of the planned MRT extension from Lebak Bulus to Serpong, South Tangerang, will remain confidential until project execution to prevent land speculators from inflating property prices along the corridor. The feasibility study for the project is targeted for completion by end of 2026, with speculation on social media suggesting possible routes through Pondok Aren or Pondok Cabe. Property developers and real estate investors in the South Tangerang corridor should monitor this project closely as the route announcement could trigger significant land value movements.

medium.title: President Prabowo Questions Whether State-Owned Enterprises Are Profitable Enough to Fund Research
medium.summary: President Prabowo Subianto responded to a proposal to allocate a portion of state-owned enterprise (BUMN) profits toward research and innovation funding, calling the idea sound but questioning whether SOEs generate sufficient profit to do so. The remarks signal presidential scrutiny of BUMN financial performance and profitability, which could influence future policy direction for Indonesia's large state enterprise sector. Investors in BUMN-listed companies should note the government's focus on improving SOE financial health.

medium.title: 8% App Commission Cap for Ride-Hailing Motorcycles May Extend to Online Taxis, Says Transport Minister
medium.summary: Indonesia's Minister of Transportation confirmed that the newly implemented 8% commission cap for ride-hailing app operators currently applies only to motorcycle-based ojek online (ojol) services, not online taxis. The government is studying whether to extend the regulation to four-wheeled ride-hailing services in the future. This regulatory development is significant for platform companies such as Gojek and Grab, affecting their revenue models and profitability in Indonesia's large gig economy market.

medium.title: Antam Gold Price Falls Rp 8,000/gram Over the Week, Buyback Price Drops Rp 20,000/gram
medium.summary: Antam 24-karat gold prices moved volatilely during the trading week of June 22–27, 2026, ultimately closing down Rp 8,000/gram at Rp 2,660,000/gram, while the buyback price dropped by Rp 20,000/gram. Prices saw a brief mid-week rally before retreating, reflecting ongoing uncertainty in global gold markets. Investors in Indonesian gold assets should monitor the continued price weakness as a signal of shifting global risk sentiment.

medium.title: Extreme Heatwave in Europe Triggers Panic Buying of Air Conditioners
medium.summary: A severe heatwave reaching 40°C across Europe has triggered panic buying of air conditioners, with viral footage from France showing shoppers rushing into stores at opening. This surge in demand for cooling appliances could benefit Indonesian electronics and AC manufacturers or exporters with exposure to European markets. It also highlights a broader global trend of climate-driven consumer demand shifts that may impact supply chains and commodity markets.
